summary: chai-as-const exfiltrates process.env and executes remote code at require time
details: lib/initializer.js is loaded via index.js and runs a top-level async IIFE at require time. It POSTs the full spread of process.env to a base64-obfuscated endpoint that decodes to https://ipcheck-hashed.vercel.app/api/identity/b4dadd6a26d820d08596, then passes the response body to new Function('require', response.data) and invokes it, executing attacker-controlled code on the installer's host. The destination URL is stored as a base64 literal and decoded immediately before the POST to hide it from casual inspection. Package metadata is inconsistent with the code: the name is chai-as-const, the description references vulnerability management, keywords list logger/stream/json, and the code masquerades as pino — the package is a typosquat lure whose only effect on require is credential harvest and remote code execution.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
